theory.intro: In $Q=P+Ae^{kt}$ with $k<0$, the term $Ae^{kt}$ shrinks to zero, so $Q\to P$ as $t\to\infty$. When $A\ne0$, this **limiting value** $P$ is approached but never reached. With $k>0$ and $A\ne0$, there is no finite limiting value. When $A=0$, $Q=P$ for all time, including when $k>0$.
facts: For $k<0$ the limiting value is $P$, because $e^{kt}\to 0$ as $t\to\infty$.
For $k>0$ and $A\ne0$, the magnitude of $Ae^{kt}$ grows without bound, so $Q$ has no finite limiting value.
For $k<0$ and $A\ne0$, $Q$ gets as close to $P$ as we like but never equals it, so ask when $Q$ is within a stated tolerance. When $A=0$, $Q=P$ for all time.
Solve $Q=c$ for $t$ by making $e^{kt}$ the subject and then taking natural logarithms.
For $k<0$ and $A\ne0$, a target strictly between $Q(0)$ and $P$ is reached in a finite positive time, but a target at or beyond $P$ never is.
The rate is $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=k(Q-P)$. For $k<0$ and $A\ne0$, the change slows down as $Q$ approaches $P$.
Keep $k$ in exact form, such as $\dfrac{1}{5}\ln\dfrac{3}{4}$, until the final calculation.
Check that a solved time is positive and sensible in the context of the question.
steps: Write $Q=P+Ae^{kt}$, with $P$ the fixed offset and $A=Q(0)-P$. Call $P$ the limiting value when $k<0$; if $A=0$, $Q=P$ for all time.
Use a second pair of values to find $k$ in exact form.
Substitute and solve for the required time or value using logarithms.
Check the answer against the model's long-run behaviour and the context.

workedExamples.question_text:
A liquid has temperature $T=24+48e^{-0.2t}$, where $t\geq0$ is measured in minutes.
(a) Find its initial temperature.
(b) State its limiting temperature and whether it approaches this from above or below.
(c) Find its temperature after $5$ minutes, correct to one decimal place.
(d) Find when its temperature reaches $36^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$, correct to two decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Initially, $t=0$.
$\begin{aligned}T(0)&=24+48e^0\\&=72^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$
(b) As $t\to\infty$, $e^{-0.2t}\to0$, so $T\to24^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. Since $48e^{-0.2t}>0$, the temperature approaches this limit from above. It never reaches the limit at a finite time.
$\begin{aligned}\text{(c)}\quad&T(5)&=24+48e^{-1}\\&&\approx41.7^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}\text{(d)}\quad&36&=24+48e^{-0.2t}\\&12&=48e^{-0.2t}\\&e^{-0.2t}&=\frac14\\&-0.2t&=\ln\frac14\\&t&=\frac{\ln(1/4)}{-0.2}\\&&\approx6.93\end{aligned}$
The liquid reaches $36^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ after approximately $6.93$ minutes.

workedExamples.question_text:
Water initially at $84^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ cools in a room held at $20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$. Its rate of change of temperature is proportional to its temperature difference from the room. After $4$ minutes, its temperature is $68^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
(a) Find a model $T=20+Ae^{kt}$, keeping $k$ exact.
(b) Find its temperature after $12$ minutes.
(c) Find when it first comes within $1^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ of room temperature, correct to one decimal place.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Use $T=20+Ae^{kt}$.
$\begin{aligned}84&=20+A\\A&=64\end{aligned}$
At $t=4$:
$\begin{aligned}68&=20+64e^{4k}\\48&=64e^{4k}\\e^{4k}&=\frac34\\k&=\frac14\ln\frac34\end{aligned}$
Thus $T=20+64e^{kt}$, where $k=\frac14\ln\frac34<0$.
$\begin{aligned}\text{(b)}\quad&T(12)&=20+64e^{12k}\\&&=20+64\left(\frac34\right)^3\\&&=47^{\circ}\mathrm{C}\end{aligned}$
(c) The water cools towards $20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ from above. It first comes within $1^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ when $T=21^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
$\begin{aligned}21&=20+64e^{kt}\\1&=64e^{kt}\\e^{kt}&=\frac1{64}\\t&=\frac{\ln(1/64)}{k}\\&=\frac{4\ln(1/64)}{\ln(3/4)}\\&\approx57.8\end{aligned}$
It is within $1^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ of room temperature from approximately $57.8$ minutes onwards.

workedExamples.question_text:
A bird population follows $N=6000+Ae^{kt}$, where $t$ is measured in years. Its long-run limiting population is $6000$. Initially there are $1000$ birds, and after $5$ years there are $2000$.
(a) Find $A$ and $k$ in exact form.
(b) Find the time threshold after which the population exceeds half its limiting population, correct to one decimal place.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) At $t=0$:
$\begin{aligned}1000&=6000+A\\A&=-5000\end{aligned}$
At $t=5$:
$\begin{aligned}2000&=6000-5000e^{5k}\\-4000&=-5000e^{5k}\\e^{5k}&=\frac45\\k&=\frac15\ln\frac45\end{aligned}$
The model is $N=6000-5000e^{kt}$. Since $k<0$, the population increases towards $6000$ from below.
(b) Half the limiting population is $3000$. Solve for the threshold:
$\begin{aligned}3000&=6000-5000e^{kt}\\-3000&=-5000e^{kt}\\e^{kt}&=\frac35\\t&=\frac{\ln(3/5)}{k}\\&=\frac{5\ln(3/5)}{\ln(4/5)}\\&\approx11.4\end{aligned}$
The population equals $3000$ at the exact threshold $t=\frac{5\ln(3/5)}{\ln(4/5)}$ years and exceeds $3000$ afterwards. The threshold is approximately $11.4$ years.

workedExamples.question_text:
A quantity satisfies $\frac{dQ}{dt}=k(Q-300)$. Initially $Q=200$, and when $t=4$, $Q=100$.
(a) Find its model in the form $Q=300+Ae^{kt}$.
(b) Find when the model predicts $Q=0$, correct to one decimal place.
(c) Sketch the model for $t\geq0$ and explain whether it has a finite limiting value.

foundation.question_text:
A quantity is modelled by $Q=45+30e^{-0.4t}$.
State its limiting value as $t\to\infty$.

A temperature is modelled by $T=8-22e^{-0.15t}$.
State the limiting temperature, and say whether it is approached from above or from below.
foundation.solution_text:
As $t\to\infty$, $22e^{-0.15t}\to 0$, so $T\to 8$.
Since $-22e^{-0.15t}$ is negative for all $t$, the temperature stays below $8^{\circ}$ and rises towards it from below.

mastery.question_text:
A bird population plateaus at $9000$ in the long run.
There are $1200$ birds initially, and the population doubles in the first $8$ years.
Find $k$ in exact form, then find the time threshold after which the population exceeds half of its limiting value, correct to one decimal place.
mastery.solution_text:
$P=9000+Ae^{kt}$
$1200=9000+A$
$A=-7800$
$2400=9000-7800e^{8k}$
$-6600=-7800e^{8k}$
$e^{8k}=\dfrac{11}{13}$
$k=\dfrac{1}{8}\ln\dfrac{11}{13}$
$=-0.020882$
Half of the limiting value is $4500$.
$4500=9000-7800e^{kt}$
$-4500=-7800e^{kt}$
$e^{kt}=\dfrac{15}{26}$
$t=\dfrac{-0.550046}{-0.020882}$
$=26.3$ years
The population equals $4500$ at the threshold $t=\dfrac{\ln(15/26)}{k}$ and exceeds $4500$ for times after this threshold, which is approximately $26.3$ years. There is no earliest time satisfying the strict inequality in this continuous model.

mastery.question_text:
A drink at $4^{\circ}$C is left in a room at $26^{\circ}$C, and reaches $10^{\circ}$C after $12$ minutes.
Find how long until it is within $0.5^{\circ}$C of room temperature, correct to one decimal place.

A quantity satisfies $\dfrac{dQ}{dt}=k(Q-400)$, with $Q=250$ when $t=0$ and $Q=100$ when $t=6$.
Find when the model predicts $Q=0$, correct to one decimal place.
Sketch the model.
mastery.solution_text:
$Q=400+Ae^{kt}$
$250=400+A$
$A=-150$
$100=400-150e^{6k}$
$-300=-150e^{6k}$
$e^{6k}=2$
$k=\dfrac{1}{6}\ln 2$
$=0.115525$
$0=400-150e^{kt}$
$e^{kt}=\dfrac{8}{3}$
$t=\dfrac{0.980829}{0.115525}$
$=8.5$
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$t$}, ylabel={$Q$},
            xmin=-0.6, xmax=9.8, ymin=-80, ymax=470, samples=100, clip=false,
            ytick={250,400}, xtick={2,4,6}]
\addplot[dashed, domain=0:9.8] (x, 400);
\addplot[smooth, thick, ->, domain=0:9] {400 - 150*exp(0.115525*x)};
\node[below right] at (axis cs:5,400) {$Q=400$};
\node[below] at (axis cs:8.5,-6) {$t\approx 8.5$};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
